notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0093.tlg010x03.1st1K: 'Πύρμηκες' is read as μύρμηκες, 'ants'. 'Often also the sharp suns, when out of a cloud' is elliptic; 'signify rain' is understood.

nodes.text: Signs of rains and winds and storms and fair weather we have written down as follows, so far as was possible, some observed by ourselves, others taken from others of good repute. Those, then, that depend on the setting and rising of the stars must be taken from the astronomical writings.

When Euboea is girdled across the middle [with cloud], rain soon. And if a cloud settles on Pelion, from whichever side it settles, from there it signifies rain or wind. When a rainbow appears, it gives a sign; and if many rainbows appear, it signifies rain for a long time. But often also the sharp suns, when out of a cloud. If ants in a hollow place carry their eggs out of the ant-hill to the high place, they signify rain, but if they carry them down, fair weather. If two mock suns appear, one to the south and the other to the north, and a halo at the same time, they signify rain soon. And black haloes are a sign of rain, and more so those in the late afternoon.
